title: Can envy be good for you? With Jens Lange, PhD, and Sara Protasi, PhD

sentences.en: Envy is a much maligned emotion.
sentences.zh: 嫉妒是一种饱受诟病的消极情绪。

sentences.en: Our feelings about it are evident even in the language we use to describe it.
sentences.zh: 我们对它的感受，甚至从我们用来描述它的语言中就显而易见。

sentences.en: We say people are twisted or consumed by or eaten up with envy.
sentences.zh: 我们说人们被嫉妒扭曲、吞噬或蚕食。

sentences.en: In folktales, books, and movies, envy is a villain.
sentences.zh: 在民间故事、书籍和电影中，嫉妒都是一个反派。

sentences.en: In the Christian tradition, envy is one of the seven deadly sins.
sentences.zh: 在基督教传统中，嫉妒是七大罪之一。

sentences.en: But in recent years, some psychologists and philosophers have begun taking a second look at this long, vilified emotion and making the case that envy is not always destructive.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，一些心理学家和哲学家开始重新审视这种长期被丑化的情绪，并提出嫉妒并不总是具有破坏性的观点。

sentences.en: In some cases, it can even be a force for good.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它甚至能成为一股向善的力量。

sentences.en: So what exactly is envy and how has it gotten such a bad rap?
sentences.zh: 那么，嫉妒究竟是什么？它又是如何背上如此恶名的呢？

sentences.en: Why are we often envious of people closest to us and how does envy affect our relationships?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们常常嫉妒离我们最近的人？嫉妒又如何影响我们的人际关系？

sentences.en: How can we learn to use envy in more constructive ways?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何学会以更具建设性的方式利用嫉妒？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: I have two guests today, a psychologist and a philosopher who both study envy.
sentences.zh: 今天我有两位嘉宾，他们分别是一位研究嫉妒的心理学家和一位哲学家。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Jens Lange, a professor of psychology at the Health and Medical University in Erfurt, Germany.
sentences.zh: 第一位是延斯·朗格博士，他是德国爱尔福特健康与医学大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: His research focuses on measuring emotions, especially envy and pride, and understanding the role they play in interpersonal behavior.
sentences.zh: 他的研究重点是衡量各种情绪，尤其是嫉妒和骄傲，并了解它们在人际行为中所起的作用。

sentences.en: He is the author of dozens of journal articles on topics, including how envy shapes social hierarchies, how personality traits such as narcissism linked to envy,
sentences.zh: 他撰写了数十篇期刊文章，涉及嫉妒如何塑造社会等级、自恋等人格特质如何与嫉妒相联系等主题，

sentences.en: and the difference between benign and malicious envy.
sentences.zh: 以及良性嫉妒和恶意嫉妒之间的区别。

sentences.en: My next guest is Dr. Sarah Protassi.
sentences.zh: 我的下一位嘉宾是萨拉·普罗塔西博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Protassi is a professor of philosophy at the University of Puget Sound in Tacoma, Washington, where she studies moral psychology and the philosophy of emotions.
sentences.zh: 普罗塔西博士是华盛顿州塔科马市普吉特海湾大学的哲学教授，她在那里研究道德心理学和情感哲学。

sentences.en: She is author of the books The Philosophy of Envy and The Moral Psychology of Envy, and she has discussed the value of envy with media outlets,
sentences.zh: 她是《嫉妒的哲学》和《嫉妒的道德心理学》这两本书的作者，并曾在各大媒体上讨论过嫉妒的价值，

sentences.en: including The Wall Street Journal, The Globe and Mail, and ABC Radio Australia.
sentences.zh: 其中包括《华尔街日报》、《环球邮报》和澳大利亚广播公司电台。

sentences.en: Dr. Lange, Dr. Protassi, thank you both for joining me.
sentences.zh: 朗格博士、普罗塔西博士，非常感谢两位做客我的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having us, Kim.
sentences.zh: 金，非常感谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Well, let me start by asking how you define envy in your work, and what's the difference between jealousy and envy?
sentences.zh: 好的，我想先请教两位，在你们的工作中是如何定义嫉妒的？嫉妒和妒忌有什么区别？

sentences.en: Because people often use those terms interchangeably, and they're not really the same.
sentences.zh: 因为人们经常混用这两个词，但它们其实并不一样。

sentences.en: Dr. Lange, why don't you take that one?
sentences.zh: 朗格博士，要不你先来谈谈？

sentences.en: So envy is initially a painful feeling resulting from an unflattering comparison with another person.
sentences.zh: 因此，嫉妒最初是一种痛苦的感觉，源于与另一个人的不体面比较。

sentences.en: And so this higher-ranked person is superior in the domain of high personal relevance to the lower-ranked person.
sentences.zh: 这种排名较高的人在对排名较低的人具有高度个人相关性的领域中更具优势。

sentences.en: So I'm, for instance, or I can be envious of Sarah's amazing book on envy, right, because I'm a scientist, this is personally relevant,
sentences.zh: 所以，比如说我，或者我可以嫉妒萨拉关于嫉妒的出色著作，对吧？因为我是一名科学家，这与我个人息息相关，

sentences.en: but I wouldn't be envious of Leonardo DiCaprio's acting skills because I'm not an actor.
sentences.zh: 但我不会嫉妒莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥的演技，因为我不是演员。
zh_words: 嫉妒莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥

sentences.en: So envy occurs when someone else has something that a person desires.
sentences.zh: 所以，当别人拥有某个人渴望得到的东西时，嫉妒就会产生。

sentences.en: And in contrast, jealousy occurs when a person is afraid of losing something that they already have, so typically a romantic partner.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，当我们害怕失去自己已经拥有的东西时，就会产生妒忌，通常是指伴侣。

sentences.en: Dr. Protassi, you've written about four different types of envy.
sentences.zh: 普罗塔西博士，你曾撰文论述过四种不同类型的嫉妒。

sentences.en: What are they, and what do they tell us about the different ways that envy can show up in our lives?
sentences.zh: 它们是什么？它们向我们揭示了嫉妒在我们生活中表现出来的哪些不同方式？

sentences.en: So it's funny because I was also planning to use my envy for Jens as an example.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的，因为我本来也计划把对延斯的嫉妒作为例子。

sentences.en: And so he stole my idea, and now I'm very envious of that.
sentences.zh: 结果他抢了我的想法，现在我为此感到非常嫉妒。

sentences.en: So let's take the example of professional envy, right?
sentences.zh: 那么我们以职业嫉妒为例，好吗？

sentences.en: And as Jens beautifully explained, envy is this unpleasant, aversive response to some kind of perceived inferiority or disadvantage vis-a-vis a similar other.
sentences.zh: 正如延斯精彩地解释的那样，嫉妒是对与自己相似的他人产生的一种令人不快、带有厌恶感的反应，源于某种觉察到的不如人或处于劣势的感觉。

sentences.en: So Jens and I are roughly the same age, the same occupation.
sentences.zh: 我和延斯的年纪大致相当，职业也一样。

sentences.en: And so even though he's a man, I'm a woman, there's going to be some other differences, but I can perceive him as similar to me.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管他是男性，我是女性，彼此会有一些其他差异，但我可以认为他与我很相似。

sentences.en: And I can envy him with regard to a good that is relevant to my sense of identity and such as, for instance, academic success, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我会在与我的身份认同相关的方面嫉妒他，比如学术成功，对吧？

sentences.en: So I envy the fact that he is a renowned expert on envy, and he has many more publications than me.
sentences.zh: 所以我嫉妒他成为了著名的嫉妒问题专家，并且他发表的论文比我多得多。

sentences.en: I may have a book, but he has many, many publications, right?
sentences.zh: 我可能有一本书，但他有很多很多出版物，对吧？

sentences.en: But now there are some other conditions that, so this is kind of the background, just envy in general.
sentences.zh: 但现在还有一些其他条件，所以这算是一种背景，也就是一般的嫉妒。

sentences.en: Situation, right?
sentences.zh: 具体情境，对吧？

sentences.en: But then in my work, I present a model that is not meant to be cross-cultural.
sentences.zh: 但在我的工作中，我提出了一个并不旨在跨文化通用的模型。

sentences.en: It's meant to characterize the kinds of envy that contemporary people in Western society is my, like Jens and I, my experience.
sentences.zh: 它是为了描述当代西方社会中人们的那种嫉妒，就像我和延斯一样，也就是我的经验。

sentences.en: Now, imagine that I am really concerned with being a good researcher, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，假设我真的很在意自己是不是一个优秀的研究者，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that's something that is at the core of my identity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我核心身份认同的一部分。

sentences.en: I really care about that.
sentences.zh: 我真的很在乎这一点。

sentences.en: And I envy Jens, but what I'm mostly concerned is, okay, I am not as good as Jens, and his academic excellence exacerbates my pain.
sentences.zh: 我嫉妒延斯，但我最在乎的是，好吧，我不如延斯优秀，他的学术卓越加剧了我的痛苦。

sentences.en: But it's not the main focus of concern for me.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是我关注的核心焦点。

sentences.en: It's just that the fact that he's similar to me is a sort of, as Aristotle would say, it's a reproach to me, right?
sentences.zh: 只是他与我相似这一事实，用亚里士多德的话来说，是对我的一种责备，对吧？

sentences.en: Why I haven't been able to be as productive, but mostly what I care about is becoming better as a researcher.
sentences.zh: 为什么我没能像他那样产出丰硕？但大部分我所关心的，还是提升自己作为研究者的能力。

sentences.en: And let's suppose that I'm a fairly self-confident person, and then thanks to Jens' generosity in, you know, he has maybe shown me how to be a successful researcher,
sentences.zh: 假设我是一个相当自信的人，然后由于延斯的慷慨，你知道的，他可能向我展示了如何成为一名成功的研究者，

sentences.en: I feel confident that I can improve my situation, that I can emulate Jens and become a better researcher myself.
sentences.zh: 我感到自信，觉得自己能够改善现状，可以效仿延斯，让自己也成为一名更好的研究者。

sentences.en: And so I feel what I call emulative envy, which is still painful, right?
sentences.zh: 于是我感受到了我所谓的“效仿性嫉妒”，这仍然是痛苦的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's still a perception of my inferiority compared to this other person, but there is hope.
sentences.zh: 因为它依然是对自己不如这个人的感知，但其中包含了希望。

sentences.en: It's a productive emotion that motivates me to self-improve.
sentences.zh: 这是一种富有成效的情绪，它激励我去自我完善。

sentences.en: Now, let's change the example a little bit.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们稍微改变一下这个例子。

sentences.en: Imagine that I'm actually fairly insecure, or perhaps I'm in a difficult work situation.
sentences.zh: 假设我其实相当不自信，或者我可能正处于一个艰难的工作环境中。

sentences.en: I have a lot of teaching in my institution, and I start fretting, and I'm like, oh no, oh my god, I will never be able to be as good as Jens as a researcher.
sentences.zh: 我在单位里有大量的教学任务，我开始焦虑不安，心想：天哪，天啊，我永远也无法像延斯那样成为一名优秀的研究者了。

sentences.en: And so even though it's not like I'm hostile to Jens, I start feeling like, yeah, maybe I shouldn't talk to him as much, otherwise I feel bad about myself.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管我对延斯并没有敌意，但我开始觉得：是的，也许我不该跟他聊得那么多，否则我会觉得自己很糟。

sentences.en: I start withdrawing from the relationship, I start sulking a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我开始从这段关系中抽离，开始生点闷气。

sentences.en: And I feel this kind of self-defeating emotion where I want to have something that I perceive as unattainable.
sentences.zh: 我感受到了这种自我打击的情绪，我想得到某种我自认为无法企及的东西。

sentences.en: And this is what I call, this is the unproductive version of emulative envy, and I've called it inert envy.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的——这是效仿性嫉妒中不具成效的版本，我称之为“惰性嫉妒”。

sentences.en: And I think this, for instance, applies well to cases of like baby envy, where there is someone who wants to have a biological child.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很适用于比如渴望生孩子的情况，就是有些人想要一个亲生孩子。

sentences.en: And that's really tough sometimes, right?
sentences.zh: 而这有时真的很艰难，对吧？

sentences.en: Sometimes it's just a matter of like what your body can and cannot do.
sentences.zh: 有时这纯粹取决于你的身体能做什么、不能做什么。

sentences.en: And it's not like you want other people to lose their children, God forbid, right?
sentences.zh: 并不是说你希望别人失去他们的孩子，上帝保佑，对吧？

sentences.en: But maybe you stop hanging out with your friends with children because it's a little too painful.
sentences.zh: 但你可能不再和那些有孩子的朋辈聚在一起了，因为这实在有点太痛苦了。

sentences.en: Now, imagine instead that, you know, maybe I've known Jens for a long time, maybe we're childhood friends, and I've always kind of, he was always so successful when I wasn't.
sentences.zh: 现在，反过来想象一下，你知道的，也许我和延斯认识很久了，也许我们是童年好友，我一直觉得……他总是那么成功，而我却不是。

sentences.en: That's kind of irritating.
sentences.zh: 这有点恼人。

sentences.en: Why is Jens always good at everything, right?
sentences.zh: 为什么延斯总是做什么都那么优秀，对吧？

sentences.en: And so for whatever reason, I developed this rivalry with this person.
sentences.zh: 因此无论出于什么原因，我对这个人产生了这种对抗心理。

sentences.en: And so it's not like I necessarily care about the good that I feel I lack.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不意味着我一定有多在乎那种我自认为缺乏的好东西。

sentences.en: It's just that there is this background of rivalry, and so I am motivated to kind of pull him down, right?
sentences.zh: 只是存在着这样一种竞争的背景，所以我有了想要把他拉下来的动力，对吧？

sentences.en: I want him to do less well rather than improve myself.
sentences.zh: 比起提升自己，我更希望他表现得没那么好。

sentences.en: And so maybe I will engage in these malicious behaviors that are often so salient in envy, our discussions of envy.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我会做出那些在嫉妒中往往如此突出的恶意行为，也就是我们对嫉妒的讨论中常有的那种。

sentences.en: I want to sabotage him in some way.
sentences.zh: 我想在某种程度上破坏他。

sentences.en: And then I have two options, right?
sentences.zh: 然后我有两种选择，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe I feel confident that I can pull him down.
sentences.zh: 也许我觉得有把握能把他拉下来。

sentences.en: Maybe I can metaphorically steal the good or really steal the good, and I can, you know, sabotage it.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以隐喻式地夺走那个好处，或者真的夺走那个好处，然后我可以，你知道的，去破坏它。

sentences.en: And maybe, you know, I get to, you know, take his place in a grant application somehow, but not because I've become a better researcher, right?
sentences.zh: 也许，你知道的，我设法在某种程度上取代了他在科研基金申请中的位置，但这不是因为我变成了一个更好的研究者，对吧？

sentences.en: I've operated in mischievous ways.
sentences.zh: 我是通过不正当的手段做到的。

sentences.en: And so I can steal the good.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以偷走那个好处。

sentences.en: And that's what I call aggressive envy.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的“攻击性嫉妒”。

sentences.en: Or finally, maybe I can spread rumors about something about Jens' behavior,
sentences.zh: 或者最后，也许我可以散布一些关于延斯行为的谣言，

sentences.en: and so people don't invite him to conferences or don't invite him to participate in symposium and all of that.
sentences.zh: 好让大家不邀请他去参加会议，或者不邀请他参与研讨会等等。

sentences.en: But I haven't improved my situation.
sentences.zh: 但我并没有改善自己的处境。

sentences.en: I've just spoiled the good.
sentences.zh: 我只是毁掉了那个好处。

sentences.en: I've just spoiled his success without thereby getting anything in exchange.
sentences.zh: 我只是毁掉了他的成功，却没有因此得到任何回报。

sentences.en: And I call that spiteful envy.
sentences.zh: 我把这称为“怀恨性嫉妒”。

sentences.en: And that, again, might be because I don't feel confident in, like, you know, taking away the good from him, or maybe the situation is such that it doesn't allow it.
sentences.zh: 而且，这再次可能是因为我对从他身上夺走好处缺乏信心，或者当时的局势不允许这样做。

sentences.en: So the four kinds of envy, emulative, inert, aggressive, and spiteful.
sentences.zh: 这就是嫉妒的四种类型：效仿性、惰性、攻击性和怀恨性。

sentences.en: And in the book, I talk more about, you know,
sentences.zh: 在书中，我更多地谈论了，你知道的，

sentences.en: the moral implications and also why I think this model might be helpful to think about our envy and so that we can move from the worst kinds of envy to the better kinds of envy.
sentences.zh: 这些道德内涵，以及为什么我认为这个模型有助于我们思考自己的嫉妒，从而让我们从最糟糕的嫉妒走向更好的嫉妒。

sentences.en: Dr. Long, I want to ask you if psychological research draws similar distinctions among the different types of envy.
sentences.zh: 朗格博士，我想问你，心理学的研究是否也在不同类型的嫉妒之间做出了类似的区分？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think they are similar, right, but not identical.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为它们是相似的，对吧，但并不完全相同。

sentences.en: So in psychology in general and also for envy, people typically take a so-called social functional approach.
sentences.zh: 因此，在心理学领域以及对嫉妒的研究中，人们通常采取所谓的社会功能途径。

sentences.en: So the idea being that emotions, also envy, help people dealing with certain social situations, typically social problems or challenges.
sentences.zh: 其核心思想是，情绪（包括嫉妒）能帮助人们应对某些社会情境，通常是社会问题或挑战。

sentences.en: And for envy, the problem is that someone is better off, right, or that the self is worse off in a domain of high personal relevance.
sentences.zh: 对于嫉妒而言，问题在于某人过得更好，对吧，或者说个体自己在某个具有高度个人相关性的领域里处于劣势。

sentences.en: So people want to deal with the situation, and they can do this by improving themselves, right, then problem solved.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们希望处理这种状况，他们可以通过提升自己来做到这一点，对吧，这样问题就解决了。

sentences.en: This is what psychologists often call benign envy, or they can try to pull the other person down to harm the other person's position, which also levels the difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学家常说的“良性嫉妒”，或者他们可以试图把另一个人拉下来以损害对方的地位，这同样能拉平差距。

sentences.en: And this is typically called malicious envy.
sentences.zh: 这通常被称为“恶意嫉妒”。

sentences.en: And this maps onto the types that Sarah mentioned.
sentences.zh: 这与萨拉提到的类型相吻合。

sentences.en: So she herself wrote in one of her papers that benign envy is very close to emulative envy, or malicious envy is very close to aggressive envy,
sentences.zh: 因此她自己也在她的一篇论文中写过，良性嫉妒非常接近效仿性嫉妒，而恶意嫉妒非常接近攻击性嫉妒，

sentences.en: and that is benign malicious distinction kind of misses, especially in non-envy.
sentences.zh: 而这种良性与恶意的区分某种程度上有所忽略，特别是在非嫉妒方面。

sentences.en: In general, like, my personal opinion is that envy doesn't occur in different types or in different categories, right?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我的个人观点是，嫉妒并不以不同的类型或不同的类别出现，对吧？

sentences.en: So in my opinion, emotions and also envy are kind of processes that unfold in particular social situations.
sentences.zh: 所以在看来，情绪包括嫉妒，是一种在特定社会情境中展开的过程。

sentences.en: So in the case of envy, people encounter a higher-ranked person, they experience pain because not having this is relevant to them, and then they want to deal with the situation.
sentences.zh: 所以在嫉妒的情况下，人们遇到了一个排名更高的人，由于没有拥有这些东西与他们相关而体验到痛苦，然后他们想要处理这种情况。

sentences.en: And depending on how they evaluate it, then this may become benign or malicious envy, or may lead to self-improvement or harming.
sentences.zh: 根据他们如何评估这一点，它可能会变成良性或恶意嫉妒，或者导致自我提升或伤害行为。

sentences.en: So, for instance, evidence indicates that when people consider the other person's advantage to be undeserved, then the situation is more likely to unfold towards harming behavior.
sentences.zh: 因此，例如，有迹象表明，当人们认为另一个人的优势是当之无愧的时，这种情况更有可能朝着伤害行为发展。

sentences.en: So malicious envy, and when people consider it likely that they will obtain the envy good themselves, then the situation is more likely to unfold towards self-improvement.
sentences.zh: 即恶意嫉妒；而当人们认为自己很有可能获得那个受嫉妒的物品时，这种情况更有可能朝着自我提升发展。

sentences.en: So benign envy.
sentences.zh: 也就是良性嫉妒。

sentences.en: So I find these types to be interesting and inspiring, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我发现这些类型既有趣又鼓舞人心，对吧？

sentences.en: And if it would occur in data, then that would also be perfectly fine.
sentences.zh: 如果数据中能体现这一点，那当然也完全没问题。

sentences.en: And so in our research, we took a purely empirical approach.
sentences.zh: 因此在我们的研究中，我们采取了一种纯粹的实证方法。

sentences.en: So we asked people to rate whether certain elements of this envy process applied to situations in which they experience envy.
sentences.zh: 我们要求人们评估，这个嫉妒过程的某些特定要素是否适用于他们体验到嫉妒的情境。

sentences.en: So, for instance, how much did you actually desire in the envy object?
sentences.zh: 例如，你实际上有多渴望那个被嫉妒的目标？

sentences.en: How much did you feel inferior?
sentences.zh: 你感到有多自卑？

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then we used analytic techniques that helped you to identify higher order factors, so things that group certain elements of this envy process together.
sentences.zh: 然后我们使用了分析技术，帮助你识别更高阶的因素，即将嫉妒过程的某些要素归类在一起的事物。

sentences.en: And we find evidence for these painful feelings, for what psychologists like to call benign envy, and for what psychologists like to call malicious envy.
sentences.zh: 我们为这些痛苦的感觉、为心理学家喜欢称之为“良性嫉妒”的情绪以及心理学家喜欢称之为“恶意嫉妒”的情绪找到了证据。

sentences.en: And we didn't find any other factors.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有发现任何其他因素。

sentences.en: And so just based on an empirical level, I think we cannot find these four different types, but we have a very similar distinction.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅在实证层面上，我认为我们无法找到这四种不同的类型，但我们有一个非常相似的区分。

sentences.en: So I don't think that this leads to a deep disagreement between the two of us, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为这会导致我们两人之间产生深刻的分歧，对吧？

sentences.en: But we don't find these four types in the data, and I also prefer not calling them types.
sentences.zh: 但我们在数据中没有发现这四种类型，而且我也不倾向于将它们称为类型。

sentences.en: In your research, do you find that everybody admits to feeling envy at some point, or are there people who never feel envy?
sentences.zh: 在你们的研究中，你们发现每个人都承认自己在某个时刻感受过嫉妒，还是说有些人从来不会感到嫉妒？

sentences.en: I think that people often say they don't experience envy, but in my opinion, the truth is everyone does.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们经常说自己没有体验过嫉妒，但在我看来，事实是每个人都有过。

sentences.en: You know, if you ask someone, like, are you envious, or did you ever experience envy, then they often say, no, I never did, because it's a sin, as we said.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你问某人，比如说，你嫉妒吗？或者你曾经体验过嫉妒吗？他们经常会说，不，我从来没有，因为正如我们所说的那样，这是一种罪过。

sentences.en: But then if you ask them, for instance, have you ever compared to someone else in a domain of high personal relevance to you, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果你问他们，比如：你有没有在某个对你个人高度相关的领域与别人进行过比较，对吧？

sentences.en: Let's say in your job, for instance, and then you, you know, were either motivated, or you gossiped about the other person.
sentences.zh: 比方说在你的工作中，然后你，你知道的，要么受到了激励，要么在背后八卦了另一个人。

sentences.en: And so, and I say, yeah, obviously this just happened to me yesterday, right?
sentences.zh: 然后我会说，是的，很明显这昨天刚发生在我身上，对吧？

sentences.en: So that this is, so I think if you describe it by not using the word envy, given that it is so, you know, considered to be as evil, as you said in your introduction,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为如果你不用“嫉妒”这个词来描述它，考虑到它被认为如此邪恶，正如你在导语中所说的那样，

sentences.en: and then people never agree to it, but the basic process, what I would call the envy process, this is what people have frequently experienced.
sentences.zh: 那么人们绝不会承认它，但基本的过程，也就是我所说的嫉妒过程，却是人们经常经历的。

sentences.en: I do like to think that my taxonomy has at least some empirical support, partly because I also use a lot of your work to argue for it,
sentences.zh: 我确实倾向于认为我的分类法至少有一些实证支持，部分原因也是因为我大量借鉴了你的工作来为之辩护，

sentences.en: but maybe the details of that are appropriate to another place in time.
sentences.zh: 但也许其中的细节更适合在其他的时间和场合讨论。

sentences.en: But in my experience, I have to say that when I talk about, once people are familiar with the way I and other people think about envy as not necessarily this, you know,
sentences.zh: 但在我的经验中，我必须说，当我谈论……一旦人们熟悉了我和其他人看待嫉妒的方式——即它不一定是那种，你知道的，

sentences.en: I tend to be more willing to discuss their envy and admit it.
sentences.zh: 他们往往更愿意讨论自己的嫉妒并承认它。

sentences.en: I find that a lot more people now confess their envy to me in those terms, precisely because they know that I don't think envy is all bad.
sentences.zh: 我发现现在有更多的人以这种方式向我坦白他们的嫉妒，正是因为他们知道我不认为嫉妒全都是坏事。

sentences.en: So I do think that the framing is really important, more so than the words we use.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这种 framing（构词/表述框架）真的很重要，甚至比我们使用的字眼更重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Does envy only apply to people, or could I envy a thing like your beautiful car or your expensive house?
sentences.zh: 嫉妒只适用于人吗？或者我可以嫉妒一件东西，比如你漂亮的汽车或昂贵的房子？

sentences.en: I like to think about this as a tripartite relation, where you, the agent, the person who's feeling the emotion,
sentences.zh: 我倾向于将此视为一种三方关系，即你（作为主体，也就是感受到这种情绪的人），

sentences.en: envy is directed at a person because of some kind of object, where that object that is perceived as, that one perceives as lacking,
sentences.zh: 嫉妒针对的是一个人，起因是某种对象，即那种被感知为自己所缺乏的对象，

sentences.en: and the object can be a physical object, a material object, or it can be a property of a person, or it can be something more abstract, right?
sentences.zh: 这个对象可以是一个实体对象、物质对象，或者它可以是某个人的一种属性，也可以是更抽象的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: But in the logical sense, there's always three things, the envier, the envied, and the object, the good object,
sentences.zh: 但在逻辑意义上，总是有三样东西：嫉妒者、被嫉妒者以及那个对象，即美好的对象，

sentences.en: something that is perceived as good that I don't have and the other person has, I would say.
sentences.zh: 也就是某种被认为是美好的、我没有而另一个人拥有的东西，我想可以这么说。

sentences.en: I agree, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我同意，是的。

sentences.en: And I think it would be strange to say that you are envying the car because of the car's, I don't know, nice steering wheel.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，如果你去嫉妒一辆车，仅仅是因为它的——我不知道，方向盘很好看——这听起来很奇怪。

sentences.en: Well, let me change the subject a little bit.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我稍微换个话题。

sentences.en: The two of you wrote a paper together called An Interdisciplinary Perspective on the Value of Envy.
sentences.zh: 你们两个合写了一篇论文，叫作《关于嫉妒价值的跨学科视角》。

sentences.en: What inspired you to take this look at the topic, and what can we learn from approaching it from both your perspectives?
sentences.zh: 是什么启发你们从这个角度来探讨这个话题？从你们两人的视角出发，我们又能学到什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Jens and I met in 2019 at a conference organized by Timo Breyer,
sentences.zh: 对，我和延斯是在2019年蒂莫·布雷尔组织的一次会议上认识的，

sentences.en: who had this wonderful idea of this conference that was titled Hostile Emotions, Perspectives from Philosophy and Psychology.
sentences.zh: 他有一个非常棒的想法，把那次会议命名为“敌意情感：哲学与心理学的视角”。

sentences.en: And he invited, he thought about a set of emotions, it was disgust, contempt, envy, antipathy, resentment, and maybe a couple of others.
sentences.zh: 他当时想了一组情绪，邀请大家来讨论，包括厌恶、轻蔑、嫉妒、反感、怨恨，可能还有其他几种。

sentences.en: And for each session, he invited a philosopher and a psychologist to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 每一个专题讨论，他都邀请了一位哲学家和一位心理学家来共同探讨。

sentences.en: And so that's where Jens and I met.
sentences.zh: 我和延斯就是在那儿认识的。

sentences.en: And I was super excited, actually, when I saw the program, because Jens had published these very important papers that I had read.
sentences.zh: 其实当我看到节目单时超级兴奋，因为延斯发表过几篇非常重要且我读过的论文。

sentences.en: And I was really thrilled to be part of this event.
sentences.zh: 能参与这次活动我真的非常激动。

sentences.en: And then, you know, an outcome of the conference was Timo curated this special issue of the journal in which we ultimately published this collaboration.
sentences.zh: 后来，你知道的，这次会议的一个成果就是蒂莫主编了一期期刊专刊，我们最终在那上面发表了这次合作成果。

sentences.en: And we really wanted to show how this topic has to be investigated from an interdisciplinary perspective.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很想展示，为什么必须从跨学科的视角来研究这个课题。

sentences.en: And even though, again, you know, there might be some ways in which, you know, the methodologies are different to some extent,
sentences.zh: 尽管话说回来，你知道的，在某些方面，方法论可能还是存在一定差异，

sentences.en: the kind of things and, you know, the explanations and the focus that I'm interested in might, you know, be different from a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我所关注的那些事情、解释以及侧重点，可能跟心理学家不太一样。

sentences.en: There is a lot of convergence.
sentences.zh: 但两者之间有很多相通之处。

sentences.en: And so, again, for instance, I think philosophers who work about on emotions and especially what are traditionally considered sins or vices
sentences.zh: 比方说，再次回到刚才的话题，我认为研究情绪的哲学家们，尤其是那些传统上被视为罪恶或恶德的情绪，

sentences.en: really ought to take into account the available empirical evidence.
sentences.zh: 真的应该把现有的实证证据纳为参考。

sentences.en: And I also think that sometimes psychologists can benefit from more nuanced conceptual distinctions.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，心理学家有时也可以从更细腻的概念区分中受益。

sentences.en: Yeah, what I found very interesting about this conference was actually the first time that I engaged with so many philosophers, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，关于这次会议，我发现非常有趣的一点是，说实话，这其实是我第一次接触这么多的哲学家。

sentences.en: So I never met that many philosophers before.
sentences.zh: 所以我以前从没见过这么多哲学家。

sentences.en: And in psychology, we always have this approach that we are kind of nonjudgmental.
sentences.zh: 在心理学领域，我们总是秉持一种不带道德评判的态度。

sentences.en: So we just take a concept just as envy and then we investigate it and try to find out, you know, whether it's functional or not or when it is functional, when it is not.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们只是把“嫉妒”当成一个概念，然后对其进行研究，试图弄清楚它究竟有没有功能、在什么时候有功能、在什么时候没有，

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: But then all the philosophers at these conferences are giving all these talks where they were discussing whether a certain emotion is actually good or bad or when it is supposed to be good or bad.
sentences.zh: 但这些会议上的哲学家们却一直在做各种演讲，讨论某种情绪究竟是好是坏，或者它在什么情况下应该算是好是坏。

sentences.en: And so and this is where we have actually complementary value.
sentences.zh: 所以正是在这里，我们真正体现出了互补的价值。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we try to identify what envy leads to, what it includes, you know, what this process is and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们试图弄清楚嫉妒会导致什么、包含什么、这个过程是怎样的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And there each time you talk to someone from the media, they always want to know, yeah,
sentences.zh: 每当你们跟媒体的人交流时，他们总是想知道：

sentences.en: is it good or can you change it or should we never experience envy or should we not always experience envy?
sentences.zh: 这到底是好事吗？你能改变它吗？我们是不是永远不该体验到嫉妒？还是说我们应该体验到嫉妒？

sentences.en: And this is something that psychologists kind of never think about.
sentences.zh: 而这正是心理学家几乎从不去想的问题。

sentences.en: So they cannot answer it because they don't have the means to do so.
sentences.zh: 所以他们回答不了，因为他们没有相应的手段来回答。

sentences.en: But this is something where philosophers are actually extremely good at.
sentences.zh: 但这恰恰是哲学家们极其擅长的领域。

sentences.en: So we thought that we could join forces and show how envy may work from a psychological perspective and then take different philosophical perspectives to find out how you should actually evaluate it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们觉得可以强强联手，先从心理学的视角展示嫉妒是如何运作的，然后再借助不同的哲学视角，去弄清楚你到底该如何评价它。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们先休息一下。

sentences.en: When we return, we'll talk about why we are so often envious of the people closest to us.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我们将探讨为什么我们常常会嫉妒身边最亲近的人。

sentences.en: Dr. Protassi, I want to ask you a few years ago, you published an essay about envy and frenemies, which leads me to the question, why are we often envious of people we're close to,
sentences.zh: 普塔西博士，我想问您，几年前您发表过一篇关于嫉妒与“亦敌亦友”关系的短文，这让我产生了一个疑问：为什么我们经常会嫉妒那些与我们亲近的人，

sentences.en: whether they're our friends or siblings, colleagues, even our romantic partners?
sentences.zh: 无论是我们的朋友、兄弟姐妹、同事，甚至是浪漫伴侣？

sentences.en: I mean, why can someone else's success be so much harder to celebrate when we know that person well?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么当我们很了解某个人时，对方的成功反倒会变得那么难以庆祝？

sentences.en: So it's interesting because I've seen two reactions when I suggest that you can envy a person, a beloved, a person you love.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为当我提出“你可以嫉妒一个你爱的人，一个你珍视的人”时，我看到了两种截然不同的反应。

sentences.en: People either react by saying, well, of course, obviously, this is an interesting to even discuss.
sentences.zh: 人们的反应要么是：“这还用说嘛，显而易见，这有什么好讨论的。”

sentences.en: And other people are like, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则会觉得：“你在说什么呢？”

sentences.en: I will never.
sentences.zh: “我绝对不会。”

sentences.en: That's impossible.
sentences.zh: “这不可能。”

sentences.en: If you envy someone you love, you don't truly love them.
sentences.zh: “如果你嫉妒你爱的人，说明你根本没有真正爱他们。”

sentences.en: And I think both things are true, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这两种说法都有道理，对吧？

sentences.en: There is in the religious tradition, especially, and in some philosophical approaches, envy and love are seen as complete opposites, incompatible, right?
sentences.zh: 尤其是在宗教传统和某些哲学流派中，嫉妒和爱被视为完全对立、水火不容的，对吧？

sentences.en: Both descriptively and normatively.
sentences.zh: 无论是从描述性还是规范性的角度来看都是如此。

sentences.en: But again, that's because, one, I think there are two things happening.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，之所以会这样，是因为我觉得有两件事情在起作用。

sentences.en: One is that we think of envy only in its worst manifestations, its most destructive and aggressive manifestations.
sentences.zh: 第一，我们对嫉妒的理解往往只停留在它最糟糕的表现形式上，也就是那些最具破坏性和攻击性的表现形式。

sentences.en: And so it's true that, of course, if you're very aggressively, maliciously envious of someone, the relationship will break down.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对某人怀有非常具有攻击性、充满恶意的嫉妒，那么两人的关系破裂确实是理所当然的。

sentences.en: Or perhaps the love maybe in some sense was never there.
sentences.zh: 或者说，在某种意义上，这种爱也许从一开始就不存在。

sentences.en: But again, envy comes in different forMs.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，嫉妒有不同的形式。

sentences.en: And also descriptively, unfortunately, what happens is that because envy thrives in similarity, in conditions of similarity,
sentences.zh: 此外，从描述性的角度来看，不幸的是，由于嫉妒容易在相似性中滋生，在相似的条件下蔓延，

sentences.en: and because we often are similar in different loving relationships, the similarity is different, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我们在各种亲密关系中又常常很相似，虽然这种相似的形式各不相同，对吧？

sentences.en: For instance, fathers and children will be similar in some obvious ways, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，父亲和孩子会在某些明显的方面表现出相似性，对吧？

sentences.en: Or people who are genetically related will be similar in some obvious ways.
sentences.zh: 或者有血缘关系的人会在某些明显的方面相似。

sentences.en: And also, you know, maybe they grew up in similar, you know, friends, childhood friends will grow up in similar environments.
sentences.zh: 再比如，你知道的，他们或许在相似的环境中长大——童年好友会在相似的环境中长大。

sentences.en: But even romantic partners, we know from actually scientific evidence that we, you know, similar subtracts, you know,
sentences.zh: 甚至连浪漫伴侣也是如此，我们从科学证据中得知，你知道的，相似性会吸引……

sentences.en: we tend to couple with people who have similar values and similar interests.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于和那些价值观相似、兴趣相投的人结成伴侣。

sentences.en: And so there is a lot of similarity.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里面存在着极大的相似性。

sentences.en: I want to be friends with people that I enjoy doing things with, people that I like, that I want to, you know, I am attracted to people in various ways.
sentences.zh: 我想和那些我喜欢一起做事的人做朋友，和那些我喜欢的人做朋友，你知道的，我会以各种方式被某些人吸引。

sentences.en: So we look for people who are attractive, and we are usually connected to people who are similar to us in various ways.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会寻找那些富有吸引力的人，而且我们通常与在各方面与我们相似的人保持着联系。

sentences.en: But then, of course, we might find out that they are better than us at a variety of things that perhaps we enjoy doing.
sentences.zh: 但随之而来的当然是，我们可能会发现，在各种我们或许也很享受的事情上，他们居然比我们做得更好。

sentences.en: So in the essay, I talk about, you know, childhood friends, like high school friends, where you have this very intense relationship with someone, you do all the things together.
sentences.zh: 所以在文章中，我谈到了童年好友，比如高中朋友，你和某人会建立起非常亲密的联系，什么事都在一起做。

sentences.en: But then comparison lurks at every corner.
sentences.zh: 然而，比较之心却无处不在，潜伏在每一个角落。

sentences.en: And so the trick there, and, you know, I talk a little bit more about some philosophical discussions of it.
sentences.zh: 所以其中的诀窍在于——你知道的，我也稍微讨论了一些关于这方面的哲学探讨，

sentences.en: We don't have to go, we don't have the time to go into.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要深入展开，也没时间去详细讨论。

sentences.en: But for me, the key is on the one hand to understand that, you know, actually envy is the dark side of love and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，关键一方面在于理解，你知道的，其实嫉妒是爱的阴暗面，反之亦然。

sentences.en: There are two sides of the same coin.
sentences.zh: 它们是同一枚硬币的两面。

sentences.en: And we have to normalize the fact that, yeah, we envy people we love all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们必须将这种现象正常化：是的，我们无时无刻不在嫉妒我们所爱的人。

sentences.en: And it might be hard to confess and stigmatize, but it happens.
sentences.zh: 这或许很难启齿，也带有某种污名化，但它的确会发生。

sentences.en: And if we all normalize it, then, you know, we don't feel monsters and we can talk about it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们都把这当作正常现象，那么，你知道的，我们就不会觉得自己像个怪物，也可以开诚布公地谈论它了。

sentences.en: For instance, with my husband, we have competed for the same jobs when we were on the job market.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我和我丈夫在求职季时曾竞争过同一个工作岗位。

sentences.en: We were both philosophers.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都是哲学家。

sentences.en: We actually work in somewhat similar areas.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的研究领域其实有点相似。

sentences.en: Because there's going to be times where, you know, we envy each other.
sentences.zh: 因为总会有那么一些时候，你知道的，我们会互相嫉妒。

sentences.en: But it's okay to say, you know what, I'm feeling a little envious here.
sentences.zh: 但说出来是没关系的：“你知道吗，我这会儿心里有点嫉妒。”

sentences.en: But, of course, we don't want to feel the bad kind of envy.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们并不想体验那种糟糕的嫉妒。

sentences.en: I mean, so that's where the other intervention takes place and where I think my model is helpful in understanding what are the factors that are at place.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是另一种干预发挥作用的地方，我也认为我的模型有助于理解究竟有哪些因素在起作用。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it's important to find oneself in a kind of growth mindset and think about, okay, how can I emulate the person?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，让自己保持一种成长型思维非常重要，要想一想：好吧，我该如何向这个人学习？

sentences.en: How can I, you know, if my beloved is doing better than me in this regard, what can I learn from them?
sentences.zh: 我该如何……如果我爱的人在这方面做得比我好，我能从他们身上学到什么？

sentences.en: And the beloved, the other person, can be generous and share, you know, their good fortune.
sentences.zh: 而被爱的那个人、另一个人，也可以表现得慷慨大度，分享他们的好运气。

sentences.en: And we can focus on how we can improve.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把重点放在如何自我提升上。

sentences.en: And we can also focus on the fact that when there is a loving relationship, our identity is also somewhat shared.
sentences.zh: 我们还可以关注这样一点：当存在一段充满爱的关系时，我们的身份认同在某种程度上也是共享的。

sentences.en: And so, their fortune can be seen as our fortune.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们的好运也可以被视为我们的好运。

sentences.en: Although, again, I don't think that's always the case.
sentences.zh: 尽管话虽如此，我并不认为情况总是如此。

sentences.en: I think it's also important to acknowledge that we are still individuals and we thrive in our own ways.
sentences.zh: 我认为同样重要的是要承认，我们依然是独立的个体，并且都在以各自的方式蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: And so, I'm a little skeptical of the solution of thinking just about shared identity.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于仅仅通过“共享身份”来解决问题的方案，我持保留态度。

sentences.en: But so, we can encourage the growth of emulative envy.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们可以鼓励仿效型嫉妒的成长。

sentences.en: And when that's not possible, we can acknowledge that and being a loved one is part of the human condition.
sentences.zh: 当这条路走不通时，我们可以承认这一点，并认识到嫉妒所爱之人是人类境况的一部分。

sentences.en: And so, we have to kind of love wisely and be able to, you know, forgive and forget when appropriate.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们必须以明智的方式去爱，在适当时机能够原谅并放下。

sentences.en: But also simply just have frank conversations, you know, be mindful about our hostile feelings when they arise and try to kind of not shove them.
sentences.zh: 但同时也要进行坦诚的对话，你知道的，当敌意情绪滋生时要保持觉察，并试着不要去压抑它们。

sentences.en: Because I think a lot of relationships, like my experience, personal and also otherwise,
sentences.zh: 因为根据我的经验，无论是个人经历还是其他经历，许多关系的破裂往往都是因为我们无法公开谈论这些事情。

sentences.en: when relationships break down is often because we're not able to talk about these things in the open.
sentences.zh: 龙加博士，我想问您一个与人格相关的问题，那就是某些人格类型是否比其他人格类型更容易产生嫉妒心？

sentences.en: Dr. Longa, I want to ask you a personality-related question, which is whether some personality types are more prone to envy than others.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，究竟是什么原因，会让某些人特别容易产生嫉妒？

sentences.en: I mean, what might make someone particularly vulnerable to becoming envious?
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，当人们与他人进行比较时——在高度切身相关的领域——就会体验到嫉妒，对吧？

sentences.en: So, as I said, people experience envy when they compare to someone else, right, in a domain of high personal relevance.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有那些描述“倾向于参与这种比较过程”的人格特质，都能够预测嫉妒的产生。

sentences.en: So, all kinds of personality traits that describe tendencies to engage in such a process will predict envy.
sentences.zh: 最显而易见的，就是社会比较倾向。

sentences.en: So, most obviously, social comparison orientation.
sentences.zh: 如果人们倾向于经常进行比较，那么他们也更有可能体验到嫉妒。

sentences.en: So, if people tend to compare a lot, then they're also more likely to experience envy.
sentences.zh: 其次，所有那些倾向于用卓越标准来要求自己的人格预测指标也是如此。

sentences.en: Then all kinds of predictors of people, of people preferring to deal with standards of excellence.
sentences.zh: 例如，成就动机、趋近与回避动机，还有自恋，对吧？

sentences.en: So, for instance, achievement motivation, approach and avoidance motivation, narcissism, right?
sentences.zh: 在自恋倾向中，人们也会用卓越的标准来要求自己。

sentences.en: So, also in narcissism, people are kind of dealing standards of excellence.
sentences.zh: 他们要么渴望塑造一个完美的自我，要么极力避免达不到某些特定标准，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, they want to have an excellent self or they don't want to go short of certain standards and so on.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有其他一些黑暗人格特质，比如马基雅维利主义、精神病态、特权意识或贪婪，对吧？

sentences.en: And also other dark traits, such as Machiavellianism, psychopathy, entitlement or greed, right?
sentences.zh: 嫉妒也会被那些会加剧局势个人关联度的环境所预测。

sentences.en: And envy was also predicted by circumstances that intensify kind of personal relevance of the situation.
sentences.zh: 更明显的是，比较领域的自我相关性。

sentences.en: More obviously, the self-relevance of the comparison domain.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，如果某个特定领域与我自身的身份认同非常贴近，那么我体内的嫉妒感就更容易被触发。

sentences.en: So, as I said, if a certain domain, it's very close to my own identity, then I'm more likely to experience envy.
sentences.zh: 当排名较高的人表现出骄傲时，例如，如果在某个群体中为自己取得的成就感到自豪是合情合理的，

sentences.en: And when the higher-ranked person shows pride, for instance, because if it is plausible to be proud of an achievement that you have in a certain group,
sentences.zh: 这就释放出一个信号：拥有这项成就是一件很重要的事。

sentences.en: then this signals that this is an important achievement to have.
sentences.zh: 因此，这也增加了该领域的自我相关性，并可能使人们更容易产生嫉妒。

sentences.en: So, this also increases the self-relevance of the domain and can make people more envious.
sentences.zh: 或者其他一些信号，表明此人处于低地位，这是人们所厌恶的。

sentences.en: Or other kinds of signals that the person is low in status, which is something that people dislike.
sentences.zh: 处于低地位是人们不愿看到的，他们不想处境变得更糟，因为这会对他们的福祉产生负面影响。

sentences.en: So, being low in status is something that people dislike, they don't want to be worse off because it has negative consequences for their well-being.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这些信号出现——比如，看到另一个人显得非常有威望、极具统治力，或者正在获得影响力——这就会加剧嫉妒心。

sentences.en: So, if these signals occur, for instance, the other person is seeing that they are very prestigious or very dominant or they gain influence and this can intensify envy.
sentences.zh: 还有萨拉刚才提到的一些情况，比如竞争或对立，战胜你的竞争对手具有极高的自我相关性。

sentences.en: And also, what Sarah already mentioned, for instance, competitions or rivalries, there's also very high self-relevance to outperforming your rival.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你的竞争对手表现得比你优秀，这绝对会成为加剧你嫉妒心理的一个环境因素。

sentences.en: So, if your rival outperforms you, then this is definitely a circumstance that can intensify your envy.
sentences.zh: 我想问的是，嫉妒是否是作为人类的我们生来就有的？还是说，这是通过我们的父母或照顾者，无意中、不经意间或明目张胆地教给我们的？

sentences.en: I want to ask if envy is kind of baked into us as humans, or is it something that we're taught either inadvertently or inadvertently or overtly by, say, our parents or caregivers?
sentences.zh: 有没有哪个年龄段是它开始显现出来的节点？

sentences.en: And is there an age when it begins to manifest itself?
sentences.zh: 我的第一位老板托马斯·穆斯韦勒总是说，社会比较是无处不在的。

sentences.en: So, my first boss, Thomas Mussweiler, always used to say, social comparisons are ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 因此，很难想象会有一个世界，在其中你不会拿自己跟别人做比较。

sentences.en: So, it is very hard to imagine a world in which you don't compare yourself.
sentences.zh: 比方说，哪怕你想说自己是个好人，你又是怎么知道自己是个好人的呢？

sentences.en: Like, let's say, even if you want to say that you are a nice person, how would you actually know that you are nice?
sentences.zh: 除非你知道自己比大多数其他人都更好，对吧？

sentences.en: If not, if you know that you are nicer than most other people, right?
sentences.zh: 在一个每个人都非常善良的世界里，你必须表现得比那些并非如此善良的人多得多的世界里更加善良才行。

sentences.en: In a world where everyone is very nice, then you need to be much nicer than in a world in which there are not that many people who are so nice.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都是相对的，人们总是在作比较。

sentences.en: So, everything is kind of relative, so people always compare.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，目前还没有任何行为遗传学研究表明，特质嫉妒中的多少差异是由基因差异等因素决定的。

sentences.en: But as far as I know, there is no behavior genetics research showing how much variance in dispositional envy is accounted for by variance in genes or so on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，文化影响肯定是存在的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, surely there's going to be cultural influences, right?
sentences.zh: 就像其他事情一样，不同文化在不同时期塑造了我们感受这些社会比较情绪的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: Like with anything else, you know, different cultures at different times have shaped the way we feel these social comparison emotions, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，在荣誉文化中，我们知道——比如古希腊文化或农民文化，关于嫉妒有大量的人类学研究——这些研究似乎表明，

sentences.en: So, in honor cultures, we know that like ancient Greek cultures or peasant cultures, I mean, there is a lot of anthropological work on envy that seems to show that, for instance,
sentences.zh: 我所谈论的那种仿效型嫉妒，甚至仅仅是你所谓的良性嫉妒（这两种之间有一定的重合），

sentences.en: the kind of emulative envy that I talk about, or even just what you call benign envy, which, you know, there is some overlap between the two.
sentences.zh: 在那些资源非常有限、仅仅为了维持生存就存在着激烈竞争的文化中，要找到这方面的例子要难得多。

sentences.en: So, it is much harder to find examples of that in cultures where resources are very limited, there's a lot of competition just for sheer survival.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，在其中一些文化中，才会存在“恶眼”这种迷信说法，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, and that's also why in some of those cultures, there is this superstition of the evil eye, right?
sentences.zh: 如果有人看着你、看着你的孩子或你的牲畜，厄运就会降临，对吧？

sentences.en: Where if someone looks at you or look at your children or your cattle, then misfortune happens, right?
sentences.zh: 存在着这样一种诅咒。

sentences.en: There is this kind of curse.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须防范嫉妒。

sentences.en: And so, you have to protect yourself from envy.
sentences.zh: 但这是因为，我们再次身处这样一个文化背景中：在这里，想要繁荣发展极其艰难，资源也十分有限。

sentences.en: But that's because, again, we are in a cultural context where it's really hard to flourish and resources are limited.
sentences.zh: 所以，恶意嫉妒会更加显眼和普遍。

sentences.en: And so, malicious envy is much more salient and common.
sentences.zh: 你很难让自己处于一种能够改善现状的环境中。

sentences.en: It's hard to find yourself in a situation where you can improve, you know, how you're doing.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于我们所能感受到的嫉妒，存在着这种文化层面以及系统性结构方面的限制。

sentences.en: And so, there's this cultural and just systemic structural constraints on the kind of envy that we can feel.
sentences.zh: 不过，回到你最初的问题，金，我的确认为父母以及家庭文化自然会对这些产生影响，甚至仅仅取决于——

sentences.en: But I also, coming back to your initial question, Kim, I do think that parents, of course, and the culture in a home will have effects on, or even simply, you know, whether,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你是否具备成长型思维。

sentences.en: you know, you have a growth mindset.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，你对世界的看法较少呈现出“零和博弈”的特征。

sentences.en: You think, like, you know, you have an outlook on the world that is less zero-sum.
sentences.zh: 如果你的父母教导你，你知道的，情况不是你死就是我活。

sentences.en: If you have parents who have taught you that, you know, it's either you or them.
sentences.zh: 你必须不惜一切代价取得成功。

sentences.en: You have to succeed at all costs.
sentences.zh: 你必须当第一，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to be the first one, right?
sentences.zh: 你可能更有可能产生某种特定的嫉妒心；或者，如果你觉得父母不够支持你，没有让你感到自信。

sentences.en: You're probably going to be more likely to feel a certain kind of envy, or if you feel like your parents are not supportive, they're not making you feel self-confident.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情，我确信——当然，你知道的，这多少有点推测性质，但我希望这是一种合理的推测。

sentences.en: Like, all of these things, I'm sure, I mean, you know, again, I don't, this is somewhat speculative, but I hope it's a reasonable speculation.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们同样知道，你的环境会影响你对各种事物的感受方式。

sentences.en: And, again, we just know that your context is going to affect the way you feel, a variety of things.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这会在人与人之间造成一些差异。

sentences.en: And it's going to drive some differences between people, I think.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你的父母对你说：“为什么你就不能像你姐姐一样呢？”诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: Or if you have parents who say, why can't you be more like your big sister, or things like that.
sentences.zh: 或者类似这样的话。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly, things like that.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，类似的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, I do think that sibling rivalry, and there is some work on that, is quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得手足竞争这个话题，而且也有一些相关的研究，确实挺有意思的。

sentences.en: To some extent, I think it's pretty widespread and unavoidable for a variety of reasons that have to do with the fact that you have this very person who's similar to you,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为这相当普遍，而且由于各种原因也是不可避免的，因为你身边正好有这么一个人，他各方面都很像你，

sentences.en: and you want your parents' love, and all of that.
sentences.zh: 而且你们都想得到父母的爱，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But some parents will exacerbate it, and some parents might be able to alleviate it, depending on how they, yeah, how they do things.
sentences.zh: 但有些父母会加剧这种矛盾，而有些父母可能会缓解它，这取决于他们，是的，取决于他们怎么做。

sentences.en: So, definitely, maybe they should not say things like that, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以，绝对地，也许他们不该说那样的话，我是这么觉得的。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about a little bit more practical advice.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来聊聊一些更具实用性的建议。

sentences.en: So, in addition to parents not saying, why can't you be like your sister or your brother?
sentences.zh: 所以，除了让父母不要说“你怎么就不能像你姐姐或弟弟那样”之外呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if you yourself recognize that you tend to feel envious, what can you do with that emotion?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你自己意识到你往往会感到嫉妒，你可以用这种情绪做什么呢？

sentences.en: How can you turn it into something that is more constructive?
sentences.zh: 你该如何把它变成更有建设性的东西？

sentences.en: In my opinion, there is no general need to turn malicious envy into benign envy or to suppress your envy in general, right?
sentences.zh: 依我之见，通常没有必要把恶意嫉妒转化为良性嫉妒，或者普遍去压抑你的嫉妒，对吧？

sentences.en: Because from a psychological perspective, envy has a social function, so it helps people deal with certain social situations, in this case,
sentences.zh: 因为从心理学的角度来看，嫉妒具有一种社会功能，它能帮助人们应对某些社会情境，在这种情况下，

sentences.en: being worse off in a domain of high relevance to the self.
sentences.zh: 就是在对自我高度相关的领域中处于劣势。

sentences.en: And that's something that you shouldn't suppress, right?
sentences.zh: 而这是你不应该去压抑的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Also, I think that benign and malicious are kind of misnomers, right?
sentences.zh: 此外，我也认为“良性”和“恶意”这两个词有点名不副实，对吧？

sentences.en: So, benign envy can also be bad.
sentences.zh: 所以，良性嫉妒也可能会产生不好的结果。

sentences.en: So, Sarah also always said this is a nice example.
sentences.zh: 萨拉也总是说这是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: I can also be benignly envious of a torturer for their torturer's skills, and this would be something that's not very nice, right?
sentences.zh: 我也可能会因为折磨者的折磨技巧而对他们产生一种良性的嫉妒，而这并不是什么好事，对吧？

sentences.en: Also, malicious envy can kind of be good, for instance, when it motivates you to harm dominant others who initially oppressed subordinates or so.
sentences.zh: 同样，恶意嫉妒在某种程度上也可能是件好事，例如，当它激励你去伤害那些最初压迫下属的强势群体时。

sentences.en: That's something that's good.
sentences.zh: 那是件好事。

sentences.en: So, that was also part of the paper that we wrote together, that there is no easy answer here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这也是我们共同撰写的那篇论文的一部分，这里并没有简单的答案。

sentences.en: So, you shouldn't suppress envy entirely.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不应该完全压抑嫉妒。

sentences.en: That would be my and typically most psychologists' perspective, right?
sentences.zh: 这将是我以及大多数心理学家的看法，对吧？

sentences.en: Turning malicious envy into benign envy, if you consider that to be more constructive, would kind of require that you evaluate the situation differently.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为更有建设性，想把恶意嫉妒转化为良性嫉妒，这就需要你对局势进行不同的评估。

sentences.en: So, if malicious envy results because you think that the other person doesn't deserve their advantage,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果恶意嫉妒的产生是因为你认为对方不配拥有他们的优势，

sentences.en: and benign envy is more likely to occur when people think that they can actually obtain the envied good,
sentences.zh: 而当人们认为自己实际上能够获得被嫉妒的物品时，良性嫉妒就更有可能出现，

sentences.en: then you would need to find an intervention that helps you to consider the object to be attainable.
sentences.zh: 那么你就需要找到一种干预手段，帮助你认为这个目标是可以达到的。

sentences.en: But I'm not aware of a strategy that actually works effectively.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道有什么策略能真正发挥有效作用。

sentences.en: So, we tried a few things, but never successfully.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们尝试过几种方法，但从未成功过。

sentences.en: So, maybe Sarah knows.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许萨拉知道。

sentences.en: Well, it's more like, I do think that here, the philosophical and the psychological perspectives diverge the moSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，更准确地说，我觉得在这里，哲学和心理学的观点分歧最大。

sentences.en: And that's why I think, you know, when I talk about emulative envy, I agree it's not quite the same as benign envy,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为，你知道的，当我谈到效仿性嫉妒时，我承认它和良性嫉妒不完全一样，

sentences.en: even though some of the research on benign envy can support some of the things I say about emulative envy.
sentences.zh: 尽管一些关于良性嫉妒的研究可以支持我所说的关于效仿性嫉妒的一些观点。

sentences.en: But because in my taxonomy, I do integrate that moral perspective that you find strange, right?
sentences.zh: 但因为在我的分类法中，我确实融入了你觉得奇怪的那种道德视角，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, true emulative envy, especially when I talk about even like virtuous envy, which is one version of emulative envy,
sentences.zh: 所以，真正的效仿性嫉妒，尤其是当我甚至谈到美德嫉妒——作为效仿性嫉妒的一种时，

sentences.en: is when really the good that is solved after is actually good.
sentences.zh: 才是真正追求的目标本身确实是好的时候。

sentences.en: And so, in those cases, I think that's something that I think we should cultivate, and I think it is important.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些情况下，我认为这是我们应该培养的，而且我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: When I feel envy, it tells me that I care about something.
sentences.zh: 当我感到嫉妒时，它告诉我我在乎某些东西。

sentences.en: And so, that's the start of an introspective analysis that I think is important from a prudential and moral perspective of like, okay, am I really disadvantaged in this situation?
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一场内省分析的开始，从谨慎和道德的角度来看，这很重要，比如：好吧，我在这种情况下真的处于劣势吗？

sentences.en: Why do I think that?
sentences.zh: 为什么我会这么想？

sentences.en: Is that a correct perception of the situation?
sentences.zh: 我对局势的看法正确吗？

sentences.en: And is this really good, right?
sentences.zh: 这真的是件好事吗，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe I'm envious for bad reasons.
sentences.zh: 也许我出于不好的原因而嫉妒。

sentences.en: And in that case, I should work on my values and then see if I become less envious once I realize like I envy someone because they have a more expensive watch.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我应该审视自己的价值观，然后看看当我意识到自己嫉妒别人是因为他们有一块更贵的表时，我是不是就没那么嫉妒了。

sentences.en: It's like, maybe I should think more about whether this is actually a good thing to have or maybe, you know, I'm envious, obviously status drives a lot of envy.
sentences.zh: 就像是，也许我应该多想想拥有这个东西到底是不是一件好事，或者也许，你知道的，我很嫉妒，显然地位驱动了很大一部分嫉妒。

sentences.en: And I think I have to start from this kind of mindful self-awareness perspective of thinking, okay, what is this envy telling me?
sentences.zh: 我想我必须从这种正念的自我意识角度出发来思考：好吧，这种嫉妒在告诉我什么？

sentences.en: And do I want to endorse this envy?
sentences.zh: 我想要认同这种嫉妒吗？

sentences.en: And if it is an envy that could bring me towards something productive, then again, I can think about how can I work on obtaining this good?
sentences.zh: 如果这种嫉妒能引导我走向某种富有成效的方向，那么我可以再次思考，如何才能努力获得这个好东西？

sentences.en: And if this is not achievable, maybe I can find something in the vicinity that I can pursue that is obtainable, right?
sentences.zh: 如果这个目标无法实现，也许我可以在附近找到我可以追求且能够得到的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: And then, you know, Jens and I have some disagreement about this idea of deservingness.
sentences.zh: 然后呢，詹斯和我对这种“应得性”的概念有一些分歧。

sentences.en: I think philosophers are very careful in like thinking that some of these cases that might be cataloged as envy are best characterized as resentment, which is a moral emotion.
sentences.zh: 我认为哲学家在思考时非常谨慎，他们认为某些可能被归类为嫉妒的情况，最好将其描述为怨恨，这是一种道德情感。

sentences.en: And so when we think about justice, so that's a little bit of a different conversation where, for instance,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们考虑正义时，这就成了另一个不同的话题，例如，

sentences.en: you can have resentment or indignation or some sort of righteous anger at the success of people who don't deserve their success.
sentences.zh: 你可能会对那些不劳而获的成功人士产生怨恨、愤怒或某种正义的怒火。

sentences.en: And of course, you can also envy them on top.
sentences.zh: 当然，你还可能额外嫉妒他们。

sentences.en: But I think what's doing the moral work is the moral emotion of resentment more so.
sentences.zh: 但我认为起道德作用的更多是怨恨这种道德情感。

sentences.en: But that's, I think, again, and I do think that some of the ways in which the empirical evidence seems to show that envy is driven by resentment,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，这又回到了之前的讨论，而且我确实认为，经验证据似乎表明嫉妒是由怨恨驱动的某些方式，

sentences.en: I do think it can also be accounted by what I call focus of concern.
sentences.zh: 我認為它也可以用我所说的“关注焦点”来解释。

sentences.en: But anyway, that gets too technical.
sentences.zh: 不过没关系，这就太学术化了。

sentences.en: But I do think that this is where if someone, if a listener were interested in this kind of discussion, then I think they should look more into my book, for instance.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，如果某个听众对这种讨论感兴趣，那么我想他们应该更多地去看看我的书，举个例子。

sentences.en: Or, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: the work of many philosophers on these topics in thinking about how sometimes we should try to develop moral approaches to this situation and kind of separate it from our personal envy.
sentences.zh: 许多哲学家关于这些主题的著作，探讨了我们有时应如何努力对这种局势采取道德方法，并将其与我们的个人嫉妒分离开来。

sentences.en: Well, speaking of resentment makes me think of the concept of schadenfreude, which, Dr. Lange, you've studied.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说到怨恨，让我想起了幸灾乐祸这个概念，兰格博士，你曾研究过这个。

sentences.en: And I want to ask you, first of all, to explain what schadenfreude is for some of our listeners who might know.
sentences.zh: 我想请你首先为我们的一些可能不太了解的听众解释一下什么是幸灾乐祸。

sentences.en: But how does that relate to envy?
sentences.zh: 但这和嫉妒有什么关系呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so what is schadenfreude?
sentences.zh: 对，那么什么是幸灾乐祸？

sentences.en: So it's when people laugh about other people's failure.
sentences.zh: 这就是当人们看到别人遭遇失败时幸灾乐祸。

sentences.en: Let's say someone experiences a mishap and you are laughing at what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 比方说某人遭遇了倒霉事，而你正在嘲笑他们身上发生的不幸。

sentences.en: Then this would be schadenfreude.
sentences.zh: 那这就是幸灾乐祸。

sentences.en: So schaden is harm, a German word for harm.
sentences.zh: 所以 Schaden 是伤害，一个表示伤害的德语词。

sentences.en: And freude is joy.
sentences.zh: 而 Freude 是快乐。

sentences.en: So enjoying others' pain, kind of.
sentences.zh: 所以某种程度上就是从别人的痛苦中获得快乐。

sentences.en: So there is evidence or meta-analytic evidence, overwhelming evidence, I would say, that schadenfreude is actually predicted by malicious envy.
sentences.zh: 因此，有证据或元分析证据，可以说压倒性的证据表明，幸灾乐祸实际上是由恶意嫉妒预测的。

sentences.en: So if you think that someone else's advantage is subjectively undeserved, that's a psychological idea of it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你认为别人的优势在主观上是不应得的，这就是关于它的心理学观点。

sentences.en: So it's not from an objective moral standpoint, but when I think, I don't want this person to be so successful, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它不是从客观的道德立场出发的，而是当我心想，我不想让这个人这么成功，对吧？

sentences.en: Then this is more likely to lead to malicious envy.
sentences.zh: 那么这更有可能导致恶意嫉妒。

sentences.en: And if you then subsequently see this person fail on another occasion, then laughing publicly about this person actually reduces this other person's standing in the group, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你随后在另一个场合看到这个人失败了，然后在公开场合嘲笑这个人，实际上就会降低这个人在这群人中的地位，对吧？

sentences.en: So if everyone is laughing, if I'm laughing about this person and no one else disagrees, then this person can't be so cool, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果大家都笑了，如果我嘲笑这个人而其他人没有异议，那么这个人就没那么酷了，对吧？

sentences.en: So this is one way how malicious envy can help reduce the problem so the other person is no longer a social comparison standard of high standing, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这是恶意嫉妒帮助减轻问题的一种方式，这样对方就不再是高地位的社会比较标准了，对吧？

sentences.en: This person has been laughed at by me and ideally other people.
sentences.zh: 这个人被我和理想中的其他人嘲笑过了。

sentences.en: So this process is most likely for what we call dominant others, so people who initially gained influence in a group by oppressing subordinates.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个过程最有可能发生在那些我们称之为“强势他人”的人身上，也就是那些最初通过压迫下属在群体中获得影响力的人。

sentences.en: So dominant others are more likely to be maliciously envied for their standing in the group, and then publicly laughing about them reduces the fear everyone has towards them.
sentences.zh: 所以强势他人因为他们在群体中的地位而更容易受到恶意嫉妒，接着公开嘲笑他们会减少大家对他们的恐惧。

sentences.en: So we actually argued that Schadenford's social function is to reduce the standing of the dominant people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上认为，幸灾乐祸的社会功能是降低强势人群的地位。

sentences.en: So yeah, from a functional perspective, and whether that's good or bad, that's a philosopher's question to answer, maybe.
sentences.zh: 所以，从功能的角度来看，这到底是好是坏，这或许是哲学家需要回答的问题。

sentences.en: Well, let me just close with one question, which has to do with social media and whether that is leading us to feel more envious.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我以一个问题来作结，这个问题与社交媒体有关，以及它是否正在导致我们感到更加嫉妒。

sentences.en: Does seeing other people's carefully curated lives online create some very distorted form of social comparison for us?
sentences.zh: 看到别人在网上精心策划的生活，是否会为我们创造某种非常扭曲的社会比较形式？

sentences.en: Is it making us more envious?
sentences.zh: 它在让我们变得更加嫉妒吗？

sentences.en: So, I mean, there is evidence that social media can foster upward social comparisons, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，有证据表明社交媒体确实会助长向上的社会比较，对吧？

sentences.en: And there's also evidence that being on social media can increase people's envy.
sentences.zh: 并且也有证据表明，使用社交媒体会增加人们的嫉妒感。

sentences.en: So there's longitudinal evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以有纵向研究证据。

sentences.en: If you are more on social media, then you're more likely to experience state envy and not the other way around.
sentences.zh: 如果你花更多时间在社交媒体上，那么你更有可能体验到状态嫉妒，反之则不然。

sentences.en: So envy is not predicting your social media news.
sentences.zh: 所以嫉妒并不能预测你的社交媒体使用。

sentences.en: But it is important to emphasize that this applies primarily to a specific form of using social media.
sentences.zh: 但必须要强调的是，这主要适用于特定形式的社交媒体使用。

sentences.en: So if you are passively browsing through other success stories, so let's say Sarah is again sharing news about her latest book or amazing envy paper on whatever social media,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你只是被动地浏览别人的成功故事，比方说萨拉又在任何社交媒体上分享她最新书本或惊人嫉妒论文的消息，

sentences.en: let's say on Instagram, you know, then, and I'm browsing through my content and I see this.
sentences.zh: 比如说在Instagram上，你知道的，然后，当我浏览我的内容并看到了这个。

sentences.en: And this can lead to a social comparison and subsequently envy.
sentences.zh: 这就会导致社会比较，并随之产生嫉妒。

sentences.en: But if people, for instance, passively browse through a news content or like actively engage in social media by like posting something on Instagram themselves,
sentences.zh: 但如果人们，例如，被动浏览新闻内容，或者通过自己在Instagram上发帖等方式主动参与社交媒体，

sentences.en: this is not making people envy.
sentences.zh: 这并不会让人产生嫉妒。

sentences.en: And also this relationship between passive use in highly self-relevant domains, whether this leads to more envy also depends on personality characteristics.
sentences.zh: 此外，被动使用与高度自我相关领域之间的这种关系，是否会导致更多的嫉妒，也取决于个性特征。

sentences.en: For instance, a review found that social comparison orientation is a personality predictor of these relationships, which means that only for people who tend to compare a lot,
sentences.zh: 例如，一项综述发现，社会比较倾向是这些关系的一个人格预测指标，这意味着只有那些倾向于经常进行比较的人，

sentences.en: passively browsing through to other people's success stories on social media actually leads to more envy.
sentences.zh: 被动浏览社交媒体上别人的成功故事才会真正导致更多的嫉妒。

sentences.en: So as usual, it is, you know, the evidence is mixed and very nuanced.
sentences.zh: 所以和往常一样，你知道的，这些证据是复杂的、非常微妙的。

sentences.en: So claiming that these few more state envy experiences then produce kind of a general rise in disposition of envy.
sentences.zh: 因此，声称这少数几次状态嫉妒的体验会继而产生普遍倾向性嫉妒的上升。

sentences.en: I think this conclusion is not warranted.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个结论是没有根据的。

sentences.en: So at least there is no direct evidence for this.
sentences.zh: 至少目前还没有直接的证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: So my personal impression is that social media is just one specific context in which envy can occur,
sentences.zh: 所以我个人的印象是，社交媒体只是嫉妒可能发生的一个特定背景，

sentences.en: but now that it kind of increases people's propensity to be more envious in general.
sentences.zh: 而不是说它在某种程度上增加了人们总体上变得更加嫉妒的倾向。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我要感谢两位于今天做客节目。

sentences.en: I think this has been very interesting, and I really loved having the two perspectives, philosophical and psychological.
sentences.zh: 我认为这期节目非常有趣，我真的很喜欢哲学和心理学这两种不同的视角。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
